summary: What is happening Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, bought no bitcoin in the week of October 19 to 25. Instead it spent $204.9 million buying back its own STRC preferred shares, according to its October 26 filing with the SEC. Social media accounts have run with the next step: Michael Saylor is "set to resume heavy Bitcoin buying" once STRC gets back to $100. That claim rests on a real, stated plan. What STRC is and why $100 matters STRC, nicknamed Stretch, is a perpetual preferred share with a variable dividend that Strategy pays monthly. The dividend is adjusted to keep the price anchored near its $100 par value, and Strategy raised the rate to 12% during the summer slump. The $100 level matters because Strategy has said it will not sell new STRC below par. Above it, STRC becomes a fundraising tool again: Strategy can sell shares into the market and use the cash to buy bitcoin. The proposed market should generate meaningful additional activity and contribute to the ecosystem’s economics, strengthening the bullish case for the HYPE token. title: US initial jobless claims 194K vs 199K expected
summary: Prior 194K (revised to 195K) Continuing claims 1701K vs 1720K expected Prior 1728K (revised to 1722K) US initial jobless claims came in at 194K versus 199K expected, while continuing claims fell to 1.701 million against expectations of 1.720 million. The previous readings were revised to 195K and 1.722 million, respectively. US Jobless Claims measure the number of people filing for unemployment benefits and provide a timely indicator of labour market conditions. Initial claims track new applications and offer insight into layoffs, while continuing claims measure the number of people still receiving benefits, providing clues about how easily unemployed workers find new jobs. The report points to continued labour market resilience, with both initial and continuing claims coming in below expectations. The decline in initial claims suggests that layoffs remain limited, while the drop in continuing claims indicates that people are finding jobs quicker. The data reinforces the picture of a resilient labour market. With economic activity remaining strong and persistent inflationary pressures, the Fed might need to step up its game and tighten policy faster. This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

title: Trump administration in ongoing talks for a temporary peace deal with Iran - Semafor
summary: According to Semafor , the Trump administration is involved in discussions aimed at securing a temporary peace deal. Vice President JD Vance has reportedly sent a letter to Tehran in an effort to revive negotiations, although Trump downplayed the initiative and framed it around humanitarian needs. The diplomatic push comes alongside preparations for a potential resumption of hostilities. An administration official told Semafor that US forces could resume combat operations shortly after the midterm elections, with the military reportedly requiring only presidential authorization. However, there is no consensus within the administration on the merits of renewed strikes. Several officials remain skeptical about escalating the conflict, while Trump is reportedly the most open to military action, despite still having reservations. A diplomatic breakthrough could ease geopolitical risk and energy prices, while a renewed military escalation could reignite concerns over regional stability and disruptions to energy supplies. Oil prices dropped after the news and risk sentiment improved slightly, but keep in mind that there's no new information in the Semafor report as it just highlights the current state of affairs. This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

title: Iran's Ghalibaf: Progress can only be achieved once the seven conditions have been agreed upon
summary: Iran this week has repeated its 'seven conditions' several times and most of it was part of the agreement with the US from June 17. Here is a recap: 1. End military operations on all fronts. A permanent halt to attacks against Iran and allied groups, including in Lebanon, Yemen, Iraq and the Palestinian territories. 2. Release frozen Iranian assets. Unfreeze Iranian money held overseas, with approximately $12 billion identified in subsequent negotiations. 3. Lift the US naval blockade. End restrictions on Iranian ports, tankers and commercial shipping. 4. Remove economic and political sanctions. Restore Iran's ability to export oil and conduct international financial transactions. 5. Withdraw US naval and air forces from the region. End the American military deployments and operations that Tehran regards as threatening Iran. 6. Pay war reparations. Compensate Iran for damage inflicted during the 2025 and 2026 conflicts. 7. End threats and hostile interference. Stop military threats, hostile rhetoric and what Tehran considers interference in its internal affairs. The US is demanding action on the nuclear to file to go along with whatever it's prepared to do in terms of those conditions. For me, this doesn't sound like Iran is particularly worried about fresh US strikes but everyone talks tough before going to the negotiating table. WTI crude oil was last down $1.17 to $101.60.
